checks: Matched 3ebb848426a73808 §1, (2)–(3). The frozen result preserves the strict greater-than count and does not claim the coordinate-count theorem for all convex bodies.

For a specified j-coordinate violation the translation of the selected barycentrics leaves total mass 1−j/N. The relative d-volume scales by the dth power. Weakening strict inequalities changes only null hyperplanes, including the singleton at j=N.

Omitting one free coordinate gives coordinate Jacobian cancellation and leaves k−1 independent nonnegative free coordinates. Their simplex volume is the stated power divided by (k−1)!. For r=N the sum-one constraint forces every coordinate to equal 1/N.

An explicit point with all coordinates positive and constrained coordinates below 1/N proves full dimension for r<N. Constrained coordinates attain their ceiling by filling a free coordinate, and each free vertex is feasible.

Independent exact polynomial integration agreed with inclusion-exclusion on all 88 cases with 2≤N≤12 and 0≤r≤N. It also reproduced the accepted rational ratio 29158754625/562949953421312 at N=16, r=13.
